title: Chain representative for ordinary pro-etale module cohomology pullback
statement:
Let $h:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], and let $A$ be a finite commutative ring. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], constant coefficient sheaves $A_X,A_Y$ and the canonical structure isomorphism $h^{-1}A_Y\cong A_X$ [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map]. Write $h^*\dashv h_*$ and $Lh^*\dashv Rh_*$ for the module adjunctions of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]; $h^*$ is exact and $Lh^*$ is its termwise derived functor. For $T=X,Y$, let $\Gamma_T$ be global sections of module sheaves, valued in $A$-modules, and define $R\Gamma_T(Q_TK)=Q_A\Gamma_T I(K)$ using K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], where $Q_T$ and $Q_A$ are localization of cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $I$ be a K-injective complex of $A_Y$-modules, $J$ a K-injective complex of $A_X$-modules, and $j:h^*I\to J$ any chain map. Denote the canonical comparisons by $a_I:R\Gamma_Y(Q_YI)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_A\Gamma_YI$, $a_J:R\Gamma_X(Q_XJ)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_A\Gamma_XJ$ and $c_I:Lh^*(Q_YI)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_X(h^*I)$. Let $e_{h,F}:\Gamma_YF\to\Gamma_X(h^*F)$ be the sheaf-adjunction unit followed by the terminal-object identification $\Gamma_Yh_*\cong\Gamma_X$, and put $w=\Gamma_X(j)\circ e_{h,I}$, degree by degree. Write $\eta_h$ for the derived adjunction unit and $\lambda_{h,N}:R\Gamma_Y(Rh_*N)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_XN$ for the canonical derived terminal-object (Leray) identification. Then the following equality holds in $D(A)$:
$$
 a_J^{-1}\circ Q_A(w)\circ a_I
 =R\Gamma_X(Q_X(j)\circ c_I)\circ\lambda_{h,Lh^*(Q_YI)}\circ R\Gamma_Y(\eta_{h,Q_YI}).
$$
No quasi-isomorphism hypothesis on $j$ is required.

proof.text:
Put $M=Q_YI$, $P=Lh^*M$, and $f=Q_X(j)\circ c_I:P\to Q_XJ$. Write $\eta^{\mathrm{sh}}$ for the underived module unit. By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], $h^*$ is exact and left adjoint to $h_*$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] with $v=h^*$, $u=h_*$: the complex $H=h_*J$ is K-injective in $\operatorname{Mod}(A_Y)$. The small-site convention and [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] give K-injective resolutions in both module categories. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] to the termwise direct-image and sections functors gives their canonical evaluation isomorphisms; in addition to $a_I,a_J$, write
$$b_J:Rh_*(Q_XJ)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_YH,\qquad a_H:R\Gamma_Y(Q_YH)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_A\Gamma_YH.$$
These use the identity resolutions of the already K-injective complexes. Sections and direct image are additive; their degreewise extensions preserve shifts and mapping cones since these involve only finite biproducts and the differentials. Thus the exact-functor hypothesis of the total-derived criterion is satisfied.

The termwise adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] applied to the module adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] takes $j:h^*I\to J$ to the chain map
$$u=h_*(j)\circ\eta^{\mathrm{sh}}_I:I\to H.$$
Let $t_N:\Gamma_Y(h_*N)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma_XN$ denote evaluation of the direct-image formula at the terminal object. In degree $n$ this is evaluation at $X\times_Y Y=X$ with the same $A$-action, so for a map $v:N\to N'$ its two composites are the identical section map: $t_{N'}\Gamma_Y(h_*v)=\Gamma_X(v)t_N$. Consequently
$$t_J\circ\Gamma_Y(u)=\Gamma_X(j)\circ t_{h^*I}\circ\Gamma_Y(\eta^{\mathrm{sh}}_I)=\Gamma_X(j)\circ e_{h,I}=w.$$
The equality holds as a chain map because the identity holds in every degree; all maps commute with the differentials by naturality.

source.place: Tag 0FND (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general), componentwise adjunction; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08J6 (remark-before-Leray), terminal sections

proof.text:
Apply [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] to $F=h_*$, $G=h^*$, target complex $K=J$ and source complex $I$. The derived adjunction used here is exactly its canonical bijection, as specified by [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. In its representative formula choose the identity quasi-isomorphisms $s:J\to J$ and $t:I\to I$, and the map $u:I\to h_*J$. The value of the right-derived representing cocone at $s$ is $b_J^{-1}$, since $J$ is K-injective; the value of the left-derived cone at $t$ is $c_I$, since $h^*$ is exact. Both derived functors are everywhere defined by the operations node, so the essential-constancy hypotheses of the cited formula hold. The termwise adjunct of $u$ is $j$ by step 2. Thus that formula says the derived adjunct of $b_J^{-1}\circ Q_Y(u)$ is $Q_X(j)\circ c_I=f$. The inverse Hom bijection for an adjunction sends $f$ to $Rh_*(f)\circ\eta_{h,M}$, hence
$$Rh_*(f)\circ\eta_{h,M}=b_J^{-1}\circ Q_Y(u).$$
This is a specialization of the cited representative equation, with no invertibility requirement on $u$ or $j$.

source.place: Tag 0FND (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general), displayed canonical Hom comparison, with sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07A6 (lemma-adjoint)

proof.text:
Use [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation] with the additive functor $\Gamma_Y$, complexes $I,H$, their identity K-injective resolutions, and derived morphism $Q_Y(u)$. The representative between the two resolutions is $u$ itself. Its comparison formula gives
$$a_H\circ R\Gamma_Y(Q_Y(u))\circ a_I^{-1}=Q_A(\Gamma_Y(u)).$$
The needed resolutions exist by step 1. In particular this formula applies to this arbitrary chain map $u$, and not just to quasi-isomorphisms.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] for the ringed-topos morphism $h$ and the terminal ringed-topos morphism $g_Y:(\operatorname{Sh}(Y_{\mathrm{proet}}),A_Y)\to(\operatorname{Set},A)$. Represent the latter by the one-object site with its trivial topology and ring $A$; its inverse image on rings is the constant sheaf $A_Y$, and its module direct image is $\Gamma_Y$. The composite direct image is $\Gamma_X$, through the identification $t$ of step 2. The site-size hypotheses hold by the small representatives already chosen. In the normalization of the cited composition comparison take the K-injective complex $J$ on $X$ and the identity resolution $H=h_*J\to H$, which is permitted by step 1. The comparison $\kappa:R\Gamma_X\to R\Gamma_YRh_*$ is then represented by the identity on $\Gamma_YH$, after identifying $\Gamma_XJ$ by $t_J^{-1}$. Taking its inverse, the canonical Leray map, gives
$$\lambda_{h,Q_XJ}\circ R\Gamma_Y(b_J^{-1})=a_J^{-1}\circ Q_A(t_J)\circ a_H.$$
The cited comparison is natural in the derived argument, so its inverse satisfies
$$R\Gamma_X(f)\circ\lambda_{h,P}=\lambda_{h,Q_XJ}\circ R\Gamma_Y(Rh_*(f)).$$

Now substitute the equalities of steps 3, 5, 4 and 2, in that order:
$$\begin{aligned}
R\Gamma_X(f)\lambda_{h,P}R\Gamma_Y(\eta_{h,M})
&=\lambda_{h,Q_XJ}R\Gamma_Y(Rh_*(f)\eta_{h,M})\\
&=\lambda_{h,Q_XJ}R\Gamma_Y(b_J^{-1})R\Gamma_Y(Q_Y(u))\\
&=a_J^{-1}Q_A(t_J)a_H R\Gamma_Y(Q_Y(u))\\
&=a_J^{-1}Q_A(t_J)Q_A(\Gamma_Y(u))a_I\\
&=a_J^{-1}Q_A(w)a_I.
\end{aligned}$$
Here juxtaposition denotes composition, rightmost first. These are functoriality, associativity, substitution and cancellation of the displayed isomorphisms. Since $f=Q_X(j)c_I$ and $P=Lh^*(Q_YI)$, this is the required equality. No step inverted $j$, $u$ or $w$.

tool_uses.why: Generic exact-left-adjoint criterion proves h_*J is K-injective; the Weil unit has no resolution-preservation replacement.
Generic resolution existence on small ringed sites supplies the module resolutions required by all derived constructions.
Generic unbounded derivability and evaluation on K-injectives fixes the canonical comparison isomorphisms.

Its canonical fraction-representative equation fixes the precise derived adjunct of the chain map, including both comparison isomorphisms.
Generic unbounded derived-map computation evaluates RΓ_Y on the map between the two K-injectives I and h_*J.
Generic ringed-topos direct-image composition, specialized to the terminal ringed topos, fixes the Leray normalization and its naturality.

lean.statement: theorem proEtale_unit_leray_chain_formula {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (h : X ⟶ Y) (I : CochainComplex (proEtaleRingModules Y (proEtaleConstantRing Y A)) ℤ) (J : CochainComplex (proEtaleRingModules X (proEtaleConstantRing X A)) ℤ) [I.IsKInjective] [J.IsKInjective] (j : ((proEtaleConstantRingPullback A h).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj I ⟶ J) : ((proEtaleUnitLeraySections A Y).rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso I).hom ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map ((NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex (proEtaleUnitLeraySectionUnit A h) (.up ℤ)).app I ≫ ((proEtaleUnitLeraySections A X).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map j) ≫ ((proEtaleUnitLeraySections A X).rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso J).inv = (proEtaleUnitLeraySections A Y).rightDerivedFunctor.map ((proEtaleConstantRingAdjunction A h).mapDerivedCategoryRightDerivedAdjunction.unit.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj I)) ≫ (proEtaleUnitLerayIso A h).hom.app ((proEtaleConstantRingDerivedPullback A h).obj (DerivedCategory.Q.obj I)) ≫ (proEtaleUnitLeraySections A X).rightDerivedFunctor.map ((proEtaleConstantRingPullback A h).mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app I ≫ DerivedCategory.Q.map j)
